history.heading: Ancient Sahara and Kanem-Bornu
paragraphs: Chad has some of the oldest traces of human ancestors: the fossil Sahelanthropus tchadensis, nicknamed Toumaï, found in the Djurab Desert, is about 7 million years old. Rock art in the Ennedi and Tibesti mountains shows the Sahara when it was green.

From around the 9th century, the Kanem Empire, later Kanem-Bornu, grew powerful around Lake Chad through trans-Saharan trade and adopted Islam. The sultanates of Bagirmi and Wadai also flourished, raiding southern peoples for slaves.

history.heading: Colony and civil wars
paragraphs: France conquered the region between 1900 and 1920, and Chad became part of French Equatorial Africa. It was the first French colony to rally to the Free French in 1940.

Chad became independent on 11 August 1960. Tensions between the mainly Muslim north and the mainly Christian and animist south led to civil war from 1965. Libya occupied the Aouzou Strip in the north, and Chadian forces defeated Libya in the 1987 "Toyota War". Hissène Habré ruled from 1982 with great brutality and was later convicted of crimes against humanity in Senegal.

history.heading: The Déby era
paragraphs: Idriss Déby took power in 1990 and ruled for three decades. He was killed in 2021 while visiting troops fighting rebels, and his son Mahamat Idriss Déby took over as head of a military council. He was elected president in 2024 in a vote criticised by the opposition. Chad has hosted hundreds of thousands of refugees fleeing the war in Sudan.

culture.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: Chad has more than 200 ethnic groups. French and Arabic are official languages, and Chadian Arabic is widely used as a common language. Islam is the majority religion, mainly in the north and centre, while Christianity and traditional religions are common in the south.

The staple food is boule, a millet or sorghum dough eaten with sauces. Traditional festivals of nomadic herders, such as those of the Wodaabe, are notable. The Ennedi Massif and Lakes of Ounianga are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

politics.heading: Government and security
paragraphs: Chad is a presidential republic in which power is concentrated in the president and the military. The Déby family and its allies have dominated politics since 1990. A 2025 constitutional change removed presidential term limits.
Chad has been a key security partner in the Sahel. In 2024 it ended its defence agreement with France, and French troops withdrew in early 2025. The Lake Chad region faces attacks by Boko Haram.

economy.heading: Oil and agriculture
paragraphs: Most Chadians depend on farming and herding. Oil, exported since 2003 through a pipeline to Cameroon's coast, is the main source of export revenue, alongside cotton, livestock and gum arabic.
Chad is one of the world's poorest countries, facing desertification, the shrinking of Lake Chad, conflict and refugee flows. The currency is the Central African CFA franc.
